revised_trade.thesis: FACT: AONIA cash is 4.35 as of 18-Sep-2026; the September 30-day contract implies 4.355 (+0.5bp) while October implies 4.565 (+21.5bp) with open interest 21752 and volume 4450, the most active point on the strip. FACT: AU 3m bank bills are 4.68 and 6m bills 5.08, so the front STIR/bill complex is pricing a hike that has not printed in overnight cash. FACT: Reuters/NSW evidence dated 2026-09-16 shows stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y, volumes -18%, and Sydney and Melbourne values more than 7% below peak; ABS July employment -15.8k and unemployment 4.5%; September Westpac-MI sentiment 84.4, down 5.2% from 88.9. INFERENCE: September cash already reveals the RBA did not lift in the current month, so October is the first live month that can embed a 25bp cash move; pricing 21.5bp of that move is a near-certain October hike. The housing/labor/sentiment cluster is the transmission channel the next RBA statement has to address, so a hold or delay is a dated repricing path for October implied rates lower. UNKNOWN: whether trimmed-mean CPI still at 3.6% y/y plus an 82 inflation-gauge score and the post-FOMC/BoJ/BoE hawkish cluster dominate housing and force delivery. Sidecar already holds this exact long; paper action is HOLD. Currency-tag conflicts do not change that mechanism.
revised_trade.mispricing: FACT: October AONIA 4.565 versus cash 4.35 is 21.5bp of tightening packed into the first contract that can fully reflect a hike after a September contract that is pinned to cash. INFERENCE: that is too much certainty of an imminent cash-rate increase given the housing downturn, weaker labor impulse, and the September sentiment drop, all of which are information the next RBA decision must process. UNKNOWN: the precise day-count mapping of any hike inside the October averaging window, which the packet does not specify.
why_now: October AONIA is the first live, liquid contract that embeds 21.5bp of tightening versus unchanged 4.35 cash after September AONIA printed only +0.5bp.

The 2026-09-16 housing evidence and the September Westpac-MI sentiment drop are dated inputs the next RBA decision cannot ignore, creating a defined repricing window rather than a valuation-only fade.

Global Fed/BoJ/BoE hawkish clustering can keep term premia bid, but it is not a substitute for an Australian cash hike in October once the housing channel is already biting. AUD_UP, USD_DOWN and NZD_UP tags in the conflict bundle do not supply that Australian cash event.
catalysts: Next RBA cash-rate decision, which is the event that either confirms or cancels the 21.5bp October AONIA hike premium.
Further Australian housing, labor, CPI, or sentiment prints that force the Board to acknowledge the tightening channel before that decision.
A hold or smaller-than-priced October cash outcome that pulls October implied AONIA back toward the 4.35 cash/September strip.
revised_trade.invalidation: The thesis is invalidated if the RBA delivers a cash-rate increase that keeps October realized/implied AONIA at or above the current 4.565 packet mid, or if incoming Australian inflation/housing data reverse the downturn evidence and the Board signals an imminent hike the strip has not yet fully priced.

context_build.causal_mechanism: The RBA tightening channel is already operating through housing turnover, dwelling prices, labor, and consumer sentiment. Markets still price an October cash-rate increase in AONIA. The next RBA decision is the mechanism that either validates that hike or reprices the front strip lower if the Board holds because the channel is biting.
context_build.path_to_current_price: FACT: AONIA cash 4.35; September contract 4.355; October 4.565; November 4.685; the strip then grinds toward about 4.94 by mid-2027. AU 2Y has sold off 39.1bp over 1m to 4.999. Over the same window the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% (SOFR 3.85 on 17-Sep), BoJ hiked to 1.25%, and BoE held 6-3 with three hike votes. INFERENCE: Australian front-end pricing imported a global hawkish impulse after a local cash rate that has not yet moved.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: KNOWN: AU inflation-gauge score 82, trimmed-mean CPI 3.6% y/y, global energy-shock narrative, and a Fed that was already >90% priced to hike. NEW enough to force a decision: 2026-09-16 housing prints (stamp duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, prices >7% off peak), July employment -15.8k, and the September Westpac-MI sentiment collapse to 84.4. Those are the facts a Board meeting has to digest rather than a slow valuation argument.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: October AONIA at 4.565 versus 4.35 cash assumes the RBA almost certainly lifts cash in the October window, with still more tightening into November (4.685) and a ~60bp terminal lift by mid-2027.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The assumption that is wrong is near-certain October delivery. Housing, labor, and September sentiment imply a material probability of hold/delay, which would reprice October implied AONIA toward cash rather than leave 21.5bp of hike premium intact.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: cash 4.35 unchanged. Change: the entire 21.5bp October premium is the marginal hike-odds component, not term premium (that lives further out toward 4.94). 3m bank bills at 4.68 line up with November AONIA 4.685, confirming the hike is in the front money-market stack, not a 10Y duration story. AU 2s10s at 34.9bp is not the driver.

historical_reference.distribution: FACT: AU 2Y/5Y/10Y are all ~99th percentile on 1y and 5y windows after a 1m sell-off of 26-39bp. October AONIA is 21.5bp above cash; September is not. Percentiles flag how far the hiking narrative has already been capitalized in bonds; they are not the trade.
analogs: Prior RBA cycles in which dwelling prices and transaction volumes cracked while inflation was still above target, and the Board delayed or stopped hiking because the housing credit channel was doing the tightening. The packet's own housing note frames the stamp-duty hole as pandemic-sized, which is the closest named analog in the frozen evidence.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Unlike a garden-variety housing pause, today's AU inflation-gauge score is 82, trimmed mean is still 3.6%, the Fed has just hiked, BoJ is at a 31-year high, and the desk thesis says the energy shock is constraining global easing. Those differences keep October-hike odds alive and cap conviction.

Cross-market policy paths: SOFR already jumped to 3.85 after a delivered Fed hike with more hikes in SR3; CORRA still starts at 2.29 with a long hiking path. Australia is the market that has priced a near-term hike without moving cash — the discrepancy to close.
